Three steps.
Then get on with it.

01

Find your hardware.

Add a device, give it a useful name, and move a control to confirm the right interface. Add another directly from the mapping editor.

02

Tell it what to do.

Choose the control, behavior and output. Start simple. Calibration, conditions and specific output choices are there when you need them.

03

Bind it. Make it yours.

Use the countdown to send a virtual test input. Save the profile, start outputs and verify the binding in your game.

06 / FAIR QUESTIONS

Before you
plug in.

A little clarity beats another forum rabbit hole.

Ask on GitHub
Is RigLogic really free?+

RigLogic is being prepared as a free Windows app. You won’t need an account or a subscription to map controls, filter inputs or use the monitors.

Is this only for sim racing?+

No. Use the same axis, button, switch and encoder tools with other supported Windows controllers. Map a flight panel to virtual buttons, or a USB button pad to the shortcuts you use every day.

The target application needs to accept the keyboard or virtual-controller input you configure.

What do I need on my PC?+

A Windows x64 PC and a supported controller. Virtual buttons and axes need a compatible x64 vJoy installation; keyboard shortcuts don’t. The Windows player package includes the .NET runtime.

Install and configure vJoy separately if you need virtual outputs. RigLogic won’t change your existing driver setup.

Will it work with every game?+

Compatibility depends on the game, controller and driver. The game needs to accept the virtual joystick or keyboard commands you choose. Use the binding assistant to assign an output, then check it in the game.

For a handbrake wired through a wheelbase, keep the wheelbase visible for native steering and force feedback. Bind the processed handbrake separately, without a second raw handbrake binding.

What does the overlay actually measure?+

It shows the output RigLogic submits—not confirmation that the game received it. Red means active or recently active, gray means quiet, and amber means monitoring is unavailable. Each overlay stays with its own mapping.

Use borderless or windowed mode. Exclusive fullscreen and protected display modes can cover desktop overlays.

Will it forget everything if I move a USB cable?+

RigLogic uses the hardware identifiers available to it, rather than relying only on the USB port. When a device needs to be associated again, you can reconnect its saved entry without rebuilding all its mappings.

Identical devices without unique identifiers may still need your help. Existing virtual assignments stay put when you add, rename or disable mappings.

Does replay send my recording back to the game?+

No. Filter lab replay compares settings offline; it never sends the recording to a game. Inspect raw, calibrated, filtered and submitted signals on one timeline, then choose whether to apply a change.

Record for up to 30 minutes, subject to the event limit. Save a recording before closing the app to keep it.

THE SHORT ROUTE TO BETTER INPUTS

Your first mapping.

01

Open the player app.

When the public Windows package is available, extract it to a writable folder and open RigLogic.exe. Keep its files together. A new launch starts with outputs stopped.

02

Add the real device.

Click + → Add device. Give it a name, then move a control to confirm the correct interface. You can also add it from the mapping editor’s Device dropdown.

03

Choose control → behavior → output.

Detect the control, choose a held command, tap or axis behavior, then a virtual output or keyboard command. Virtual outputs need a compatible x64 vJoy installation. Manage virtual-output settings under Settings.

04

Calibrate. Bind. Verify.

For an axis, capture released and full travel. Set a deadzone on that calibrated range. Use … → Bind in game… for a countdown-generated virtual test input. Keep physical controls still; the helper cannot hide a visible raw controller.

05

Save it, then watch it.

Save the mapping and profile, start outputs, and confirm the binding in the target game. Watch pins an independent overlay. Filter lab records the selected analog mapping for offline inspection. Save traces before exiting.

Before driving

Pause rig motion during setup. Keep a wheelbase visible for native steering and force feedback. RigLogic’s output cleanup is not your motion platform’s emergency stop.

Need help? Include your version and diagnostics

NOTHING TO SIGN INTO

A website.
Not another account.

This site has no analytics, advertising scripts, tracking pixels or contact forms. The interactive demos use simulated input and never access your hardware.

Your animation preference may be saved in local browser storage. No recording is uploaded. Links to GitHub leave this site and are subject to GitHub’s own policies. A hosting provider can process ordinary connection logs.

RigLogic app diagnostics can include controller names, profile labels and file paths. Review them before sharing a support archive.
